summary_html: Child safely **reunified with parent or guardian**, case closed. Federal policy treats reunification as the preferred outcome once risk factors are mitigated.
authority_html:
- **Adoption and Safe Families Act (ASFA)** — establishes reunification timelines and permanency goals  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funds reunification services and tracks permanency outcomes

primary_citations.citation_text: South Dakota - S.D. Codified Laws Chapter 26-8A (Protection of Children from Abuse or Neglect – mandatory reporting, CPS investigation, central registry)
S.D. Codified Laws Chapter 26-7A (Juvenile Court – temporary custody hearings, adjudication, disposition)

regulations_applicable.title: ARSD Article 67:14 - Child Protection Services (Department of Social Services)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed an abuse and neglect adjudication of an infant with non-accidental head trauma, holding the adjudication concerns the child's status so no parent-specific findings were required, and that a parent's remedy for an erroneous central registry listing lies with the Department, not the juvenile court.
key_cases.relevance: After a period of State supervision the child was returned to the mother and the case was dismissed, the reunification endpoint.
key_cases.quote: Mother's remedy is with the Department rather than the juvenile court that is adjudicating the status of the child

key_cases.holding: The court held that ASFA's aggravated-circumstances exception to reasonable efforts does not override ICWA's active efforts requirement, but affirmed termination because DSS in fact continued to provide active efforts that proved unsuccessful.
key_cases.relevance: It defines the point at which reunification efforts may lawfully stop - when they have proved unsuccessful, not merely inconvenient.
key_cases.quote: Under ICWA, DSS was bound by law to make "active efforts" to reunite J.S.B with his father, but it was not required to persist with futile efforts.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination, holding the circuit court did not clearly err in finding that further reasonable efforts would be futile and that statutory good cause under SDCL 26-8A-21.1 and 26-8A-26.1 justified terminating the parents' rights.
key_cases.relevance: It defines the futility limit on the reunification goal and places the burden on parents to show the futility finding was clearly erroneous.
key_cases.quote: the court had sufficient evidence and reasoning to find Mother's efforts futile when considering the children's best interests

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the adjudication and termination, holding that the State proved abuse and neglect by clear and convincing evidence and that DSS need not exhaust every possible form of assistance before termination becomes the least restrictive alternative.
key_cases.relevance: The reasonable-efforts findings here define when reunification ceases to be the required goal in South Dakota.
key_cases.quote: The State has the burden of proving that the children were abused or neglected by clear and convincing evidence.

extended_foster_care_age: 18 to 21, discretionary; only if still finishing 12th grade or in remedial treatment, with written consent (SDCL 26-6-6.1)

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
